images.role: opening cognitive anchor: receipt versus reservation of a real tool
images.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: explanatory illustration embedded near the opening of a long AhaFold HTML guide.
Input image role: identity and drawing-style reference only. Transform the reference character into ONE new narrative scene; do not reproduce the reference sheet, its layout, pose collection or headings.

Scene and teaching relationship: a receipt is only a message; a reservation binds a particular physical tool. Show ONE Fold character actively attaching a short paper reservation tag with a visible loop to ONE real cordless drill resting on a low tool-library shelf. The drill remains on the shelf, not handed to a borrower. Place a separate loose receipt on the nearby counter, visibly NOT attached to the drill. Fold's paper-strip arms should be engaged with the tag/loop, its attentive dash eyes directed at the work. Only a shelf/counter, drill, attached tag and loose receipt are needed.
Text, verbatim: the attached tag reads “留置”; the separate receipt reads “收件”. These are the only requested words. Make both Chinese labels large, simple and legible at mobile viewing size, close to their correct object.
Identity: Fold's entire body is one squat apricot-yellow paper page (#F4C96B), slightly irregular dark hand-drawn outline (#242A2D), ONE teal folded upper corner (#2A8C82), two short dark dash eyes, no mouth. Short flat paper-strip arms and small paper-tab feet; no fingers, gloves, clothing, robot joints or wire limbs. Keep the same flat paper character as the reference.
Style: restrained editorial hand-drawn illustration, flat colors, clean white background, very light paper feel, generous white space, sparse objects, clear physical action. Landscape approximately 3:2. Keep all objects and both labels comfortably inside the canvas. Use one coherent scene, not a flowchart or panel grid.
Boundary: this is an intuitive scene, not evidence of timing, eligibility, inventory totals or completed borrowing. Do not draw a clock, numerical chart, money transfer, checkmark claiming all conditions satisfied, or extra caption/brand/watermark/signature. The accompanying HTML states the exact rules and limits. Preserve any provenance markings the generation service itself supplies.

images.role: chapter anchor: recorded return versus inspection, availability and settlement
images.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a second chapter illustration inside the same long AhaFold tool-library guide.
Input images: Image 1 is the Fold identity reference only. Image 2 is the companion illustration for visual style and the blue-grey cordless drill design, not a layout to reproduce. Make ONE new coherent scene, not a character sheet or before/after panel.

Teaching relationship: a recorded return stops the borrowing clock, while the physical tool still awaits inspection and is not automatically available to the next borrower.
Show ONE Fold character leaning attentively over a low inspection bench, holding a simple magnifying glass toward the same kind of blue-grey cordless drill, now lying in an inspection tray. Fold must actively examine the drill rather than holding up a topic sign. On the bench beside the tray, show a clearly visible return record card. Both the tool and card stay at the bench. Do not show a borrower taking the drill, a money refund, a damage verdict or a completed inspection.
Exact text: the return record card reads “已记归还”; the tray's front label reads “待检查”. Only these two labels; large, clean Chinese characters, legible at mobile size. Remove the earlier “留置” tag and receipt from this different stage.
Keep Fold consistent: a single squat apricot-yellow page with a slightly irregular charcoal outline, ONE teal folded upper corner, two short dark dash eyes, no mouth. Short flat paper-strip arms and small paper-tab feet; no realistic hands, fingers, gloves, clothes, wire limbs, extra folds or robot parts.
Style and framing: match the companion's restrained hand-drawn editorial illustration, white background, sparse props, flat color, only very light paper shading. Landscape around 3:2, with comfortable margins. Keep the magnifying glass aimed at the drill, and keep labels separated and clearly attached to their own card/tray. No decorative headline, brand logo, chart, clocks, numerical values or extra text.
The HTML caption will explain that the service desk must actually register the return, inspection does not by itself establish damage liability, and availability and deposit settlement are separate states. The image is an intuitive anchor, not a replacement for those precise rules. Do not add a decorative signature/watermark; preserve provenance markings supplied by the generation service itself.
